title: Typed async-iterator compatibility layer + multi-language examples for streaming + tools + structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a small, well-documented compatibility layer that exposes streaming responses as a typed AsyncIterator (TS), async generator (Py), and channel/iterator (Go), while preserving older callback-style and event-emitter integration patterns used by some customers. Also include end-to-end examples showing tool/function calling events and structured JSON emission (partial + final objects) in each language.

Motivation: Multiple customers rely on both new iterator-based consumption and legacy callback integrations. We need one canonical wire envelope that carries typed events (token, tool_call.request, tool_call.response, structured_chunk, structured_done, error, done) and client-side shims that parse and surface those events idiomatically in each SDK. This ticket creates the core interfaces and example snippets to be included in the next SDK patch release and will be used by docs and samples teams.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a single streaming envelope with event-type metadata for tokens, tool invocation start/finish, structured-json chunks, and finalization.
TypeScript SDK exposes a typed AsyncIterator<StreamEvent<TSchema>> that yields events for downstream consumers and includes a compatibility shim to accept (event, callback) handlers.
Python SDK exposes an async generator yielding typed NamedTuple or Pydantic model instances for events; compatibility shim for callback/coroutine listeners provided.
Go SDK exposes a channel-based iterator and an interface for callback subscription; Go structs and json tags for structured output validated in examples.

Examples demonstrate a tool call where the model emits a tool invocation event, the client forwards to a local tool handler, and the tool's result is fed back as a tool_call.response event in the same stream.

Backpressure strategy documented: client can pause consumption by not pulling the iterator; SDK will not buffer unboundedly (max buffer 64 events by default) and emits a backpressure warning event if exceeded.
Docs PR with three language examples and quickstart merged and linked from release notes.
Unit tests cover parsing of mixed event streams and the compatibility shim behavior in all three SDKs.
API ergonomics reviewed by DevEx and PM and any issues captured as follow-ups.
Updated_at date >= created_at and metadata complete per agents.md.
technical_notes:
Design summary: use a single streaming JSON-lines or SSE envelope where each top-level line is a JSON object: { "event": "token|tool_request|tool_response|structured_chunk|structured_done|done|error|warning", "seq": int, "payload": { ... }, "schema": optional string } . The client will parse lines incrementally and reconstruct structured JSON by concatenating structured_chunk payloads until structured_done for a given schema id.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Binary framing vs JSON-lines: chose JSON-lines for universal compatibility with browser fetch streaming and existing infra; binary delta would complicate language SDKs.
- Strict schema enforcement client-side: we validate shapes where possible (TS types, Pydantic in Py, json.Unmarshal into typed Go structs) but do not block delivery to user callbacks for partial/unknown events.
- Buffering/backpressure: SDKs provide bounded queues; default 64 events, configurable via client options.
- Tool calls inside stream: support in-band tool invocation by including request_id and tool metadata - avoids out-of-band RPCs and lets the runtime correlate requests and responses across the same stream.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Define StreamEvent union types for TS/Py/Go and wire envelope format.
2) Implement core parser for line-delimited JSON with incremental decode and chunk reassembly.
3) Implement language shims: AsyncIterator + callback wrapper (TS), async generator + event handler shim (Py), channel + Subscriber interface (Go).
4) Add examples and unit tests.
5) Docs + sample apps + release notes.
decisions: 1) Use JSON-lines envelope for maximum language compatibility. 2) Provide both iterator and callback semantics in each SDK via a small wrapper object to ease migration. 3) Perform schema validation client-side but do not fail stream delivery if validation fails; instead emit a 'warning' event. 4) Default bounded buffer of 64 events; make configurable via client options. 5) Support in-band tool_call lifecycle with request_id correlation for simpler app integration.
notes: Follow-up tickets will add: 1) schema registry integration for server-published schemas, 2) telemetry for backpressure events, 3) a migration guide for customers using legacy callback-only patterns. DevEx to review sample-forums after initial patch.
follow_up_actions: Create docs PR for /docs/reference/streaming with three language samples
Add unit tests for partial structured JSON reassembly
Add examples demonstrating function/tool call timeouts and retries
